$comment: THE LOCALE REGISTER — the one place a language is declared. [lane i18n-pipeline, O-LOCALES-HAND-TYPED-IN-12-PLACES]
Before this file the set 'en, ta, hi' was typed by hand in a dozen places across code, tests, CI,
store tooling and native manifests, and two of them were already out of step: the brick shipped
en+ta while the chassis Settings picker offered Hindi (a dead control in every new app), and the
privacy-notice guard derived its locale duty from the brick, so Hindi was invisible to K-14.
Everything else READS this file:
- tooling/i18n/locales.mjs renders the Dart table (packages/design_system/lib/src/l10n/
locale_register.g.dart) both Settings pickers and the locale-looping tests read, and every
app's native declarations (iOS/macOS CFBundleLocalizations, Android locales_config.xml +
android:localeConfig, MSIX `languages:`). `--write` regenerates, `--check` fails on drift.
- tooling/ci/assert-locale-register.mjs fails CI on a supported locale with no ARB in an app, the
chassis or the brick; on a stale generated file or native declaration; and on ANY hand-typed
list of two or more register codes in a tracked source file that does not carry a
`locale-list:` note saying why it is not the set.
- assert-policy-archive (K-14), assert-stamp-text-fidelity, the content-pack recipe, the ci.yml
chassis regen step and the platform Worker's e-mail copy.
FIELDS. code: the BCP-47 tag, and the ARB suffix (`app_<code>.arb`, `-` as `_`). englishName /
nativeName: the picker shows nativeName, so a reader finds their language without first reading the
current one. script: ISO 15924. direction: ltr | rtl. plural: the CLDR cardinal categories the
language uses, which a translation's ICU `plural` arms are checked against. status: supported (ships
everywhere, every surface must carry it) | pending (declared, ships nowhere yet). apple / android /
msix: the tag each OS manifest spells it with.
PSEUDO LOCALES are test-only and never ship: en-XA (accented, ~40% longer) catches truncation and
overflow; ar-XB (mirrored, right-to-left) catches every hard-wired left/right. Tests build them from
the English ARB at run time (packages/design_system/lib/testing/pseudo_locale.dart).
ADDING A LANGUAGE: add a row as `pending`, run `node tooling/i18n/locales.mjs --write`, translate
(tooling/i18n/translation-qa.mjs lists what is missing and writes the review sheet), then flip it to
`supported` — the guard names every ARB, manifest and template still missing it. Legal copy in a new
language needs the owner's native review before it is published (C-OWNER-APPROVAL-BOUNDARY).

pseudo.purpose: accented and expanded text: truncation, overflow and concatenation
mirrored layout: every hard-wired left/right shows up under right-to-left
